title: Motion channels a track omits reach the face as 0, not as 'no say'
body:
## Summary
`motionAt` in apps/desktop/src/lib/face-timeline.ts turns a head or gaze channel a motion frame omits into 0, so an omitted channel reads as 'centred on purpose'.

## Description
`poseOf` (apps/desktop/src/lib/face-timeline.ts:222-237) maps every missing head/gaze field to 0 with `n()`; only the lids keep `null`. `FaceSignal.motion` (apps/desktop/src/avatar/types.ts:55) and the Rust `RawMotion` (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/face.rs:28-38) require every channel but blink, so the wire cannot say 'absent' for head or gaze. The rig-parameter-contract technique ('absent is not zero; absent survives every hop') says a producer with no gaze channel should leave the face its procedural saccades, not a fixed centred stare. Today's helper (src/athena/channels/voice/face_helper/motion.py retarget) always sends all channels, so nothing live is wrong; the gap opens the day a second motion source arrives. Fixing it widens the wire contract in TS, Rust and the driver's crossfade (per-channel weights), an architecture call. Recorded as a deviation from rig-parameter-contract.

## Flow
- a motion source sends frames with head only (no eyes)
- motionAt -> poseOf fills gazeX/gazeY = 0
- the driver crossfades gaze to 0: her saccades stop, eyes held centred for the whole track

## Expected impact
A future motion source without gaze keeps her own procedural motion on that channel; done piecemeal it could break the Rust mirror and the 40 Hz wire.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - an omitted channel stays procedural instead of frozen at 0
Before: a head-only frame yields gazeX 0 for the whole track (walked through poseOf)
After: gaze stays procedural (per-channel null through wire and driver)
Method: simulation - three cases walked (head-only track; lids-only track, already null; full track, unchanged); no second producer exists to probe
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: architecture
evidence:
apps/desktop/src/lib/face-timeline.ts:223 const n = (v) => (typeof v === 'number' && Number.isFinite(v) ? v : 0);
apps/desktop/src/lib/face-timeline.ts:230-235 yaw/pitch/roll/gazeX/gazeY: n(...)
apps/desktop/src/avatar/types.ts:55 motion: { yaw: number; ...; blink: number | null; gazeX: number; gazeY: number } | null
apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/face.rs:28-38 RawMotion: only blink is Option

instrument: a test over visemes_of with a phone missing from VISEME asserting the answer carries an unknown count (or a stderr line); red today
title: Count the phones the helper shapes as 'E' because it has no entry for them
body:
## Summary
`visemes_of` in src/athena/channels/voice/face_helper/visemes.py silently shapes any phone it has no entry for as `E`; nothing counts or reports it.

## Description
src/athena/channels/voice/face_helper/visemes.py:249 `vs = VISEME.get(p, ('E',))` (and :247 for `h`). The viseme-drive technique: 'Unknown sounds fall back to a neutral mid vowel and are counted, not silently dropped' (law unknown-is-not-a-value). A Kokoro voice or misaki release that emits a new symbol would give every such phone a half-open mouth with no trace in the helper's stderr or its visemes answer, so a lip-sync regression would be invisible.

## Flow
- a token whose symbol is not in VISEME (a new IPA letter) arrives
- visemes_of maps it to E
- the answer has no field and stderr no line saying so

## Expected impact
Someone debugging 'her mouth is wrong on X' sees the unknown phones per sentence; nothing user-visible changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - unknown phones are counted
Before: 0 places report an unknown phone
After: the visemes answer (or stderr) carries the count
Method: simulation - walked one unknown symbol through phones -> visemes_of; the probe needs a symbol fixture, an S instrument this round did not build
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
src/athena/channels/voice/face_helper/visemes.py:247 vs = VISEME.get(nxt, ('E',))[:1] if nxt else ('E',)
src/athena/channels/voice/face_helper/visemes.py:249 vs = VISEME.get(p, ('E',))

instrument: a MotionWorker test with a stub Motion (no torch) that cancels N sentences and asserts `cancelled` is empty once each is skipped or finished
title: The motion worker's cancelled-id set only ever grows
body:
## Summary
`MotionWorker.cancelled` in src/athena/channels/voice/face_helper/main.py is added to on every cancel and never pruned, for the life of the helper.

## Description
src/athena/channels/voice/face_helper/main.py:131-137 `cancel` does `self.cancelled.update(ids)`; `_run` (:198-218) only reads it. Every barge-in or closed line adds ids, including ids whose job already finished, and the helper lives as long as the daemon. The set holds small ints, so the cost is bytes per sentence; the defect is an unbounded structure in a long-lived sidecar (subprocess-lifecycle: what a job opens, it closes).

## Flow
- she is cut off 1,000 times over a week
- each cancel adds the line's sentence ids
- cancelled holds every one until the daemon restarts

## Expected impact
The helper's memory stays flat over a long session; nothing user-visible. Could break: a cancel that arrived before its sentence would be lost if pruned too eagerly (not possible in today's order).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the set is bounded by the jobs in flight
Before: grows by every cancelled id, forever (read of main.py)
After: empty once each cancelled job is dequeued
Method: simulation - _run builds a torch-backed Motion; a stub needs an S seam this round did not build
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
src/athena/channels/voice/face_helper/main.py:131 def cancel(self, ids): with self.lock: self.cancelled.update(ids)
src/athena/channels/voice/face_helper/main.py:203 if self._is_cancelled(ident): continue  # the id is never removed

title: A face card whose form fails to load is a blank, still-choosable box
body:
## Summary
In the first act's Face step (apps/desktop/src/scenes/waking/face-step.tsx), a face card's `<Avatar>` has no `fallback`, so a form that fails to load leaves an empty 120 px box on a card that can still be chosen.

## Description
`canDrawFace` (apps/desktop/src/avatar/support.ts) only probes WebGL2; a form whose layers.json or PNGs fail (apps/desktop/src/avatar/layers.ts:107-124) makes the runtime mark `data-face=unavailable` and hide the canvas (apps/desktop/src/avatar/runtime.ts:163-168). Every other surface passes `fallback` (apps/desktop/src/scenes/voice/face.tsx:63, the Bell); face-step.tsx:175 does not, and the card stays enabled, so the person is asked to choose a form by watching a blank. What it should show (the Bell, or the dashed cannot-draw card of the no-WebGL2 path) and whether it stays choosable is a product call.

## Flow
- a form's PNG 404s (a broken install)
- the Face step renders: canDrawFace() is true
- the card shows an empty box and 'Owl of light'; choosing it works, and the surface then falls back to the Bell

## Expected impact
The person never picks a form they cannot see; measured by a face-step test with a failing form.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a card that cannot draw says so
Before: 1 of 3 card states (load failure) unhandled
After: handled like the no-WebGL2 path
Method: simulation - walked the failure through Avatar.tsx and runtime.ts; the card's content is a direction
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
apps/desktop/src/scenes/waking/face-step.tsx:175 <Avatar avatar={c.id} size={CARD_FACE} source={audition.source(c.id)} />  // no fallback
apps/desktop/src/scenes/voice/face.tsx:63 <Avatar ... fallback={bell} />

title: Her face pops in: the canvas flips from hidden to visible with no ease
body:
## Summary
When a form finishes loading, apps/desktop/src/avatar/runtime.ts sets the canvas `visibility` from hidden to visible in one frame, so the face arrives with a cut on every surface.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/avatar/runtime.ts:219-220 draws the rest frame then sets `canvas.style.visibility = 'visible'`; apps/desktop/src/avatar/Avatar.tsx:368 starts it hidden. An empty-to-loaded swap that jumps is the overlay's first ui-perfectionist anchor. A fix is an opacity ease on a motion token (transform/opacity only, lib/motion.ts) that collapses under Calm, but its duration, and whether a fade reads as her arriving or as lag, is judged by eye in the real window; Avatar's styles are inline today.

## Flow
- open the Voice depth with a face chosen
- the box is empty while the layers decode
- the face appears in a single frame

## Expected impact
A softer arrival on the surface, the Voice depth and the Face step; could add up to a token's duration before she is fully seen.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the arrival eases
Before: a hard cut (1 frame)
After: an opacity ease on a motion token, none under Calm
Method: simulation - needs the real window to judge (Lane C: a browser or Tauri to see)
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
